headline: Red Sox Bats Fall Silent In Frustrating Eight To One Loss
morning_brew: Absolutely brutal night at Fenway as the bats went cold and the bullpen couldn't keep the Nationals in check. We were hopeful after that early lead, but the team just couldn't manufacture anything against Washington pitching. It is tough watching the lineup struggle to put base runners together, especially when the pitching staff gets worn down like that in the middle frames. You have to feel for the folks who stuck around in the stands until the final out of that disaster.

Early gave us some decent innings to start, keeping the game quiet for a while, but once the relief work began, the floodgates opened. It is a long season, but nights like this make you realize how thin the margin for error is when the offense goes silent. My mother watched a few innings and said the approach looked completely lost at the plate, and honestly, I have no argument for her. She has seen enough baseball to know when a team is just pressing too hard.

We have a chance to put this behind us with the finale at Fenway this afternoon before hitting the road for the West Coast. We need a much better showing from the starters to give the bullpen a break after how much they were taxed during that late-game barrage. Let's hope the boys wake up and bring some energy to the park because the fans deserve a win before we head out to face the Angels.
